The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking compensation for an amount of Rs.8,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 17.02.2021 at about 1.35 pm., when the petitioner riding a TVA XL bearing No.KA-42-W-0966 on NH-209, Near Jekkegowdana Doddi village, Sathnoor Hobli carefully and cautiously and by observing all the traffic rules on left side of the road, at that time, one Fashion Pro motor bike bearing No.KA-04-HB-2519 ridden by its rider with very high speed in a rash and negligent manner came SCCH - 26 3 MVC No.1466/2021 from behind side of the petitioner and dashed against the petitioner riding TVS XL.
As a result he fell down along with TVS XL and sustained comminuted fracture end right leg both bone and other injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Kanakapura Government Hospital after first aid he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru wherein the petitioner took treatment as inpatient and fracture was confirmed and advised to undergo operation.
The Sathanoor police have registered a case against the rider of Fashion Pro Motor Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519.
After investigation, the police have filed a charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 IPC.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Fashion Pro Motor Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519 by its rider.
The respondent No.1 was insurer and respondent No.2 was its RC owner of the Fashion Pro Motor Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519.
Hence, both are jointly and severally liable for payment of compensation of SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.1466/2021 Rs.8,00,000/- from the respondents.
3. After service of summons, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court and hence, he has been placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 has appeared through his counsel and filed the objections to main petition.
Respondent No.1 - Insurance Company filed its objection that the denying the petition averments.

Respondent has admitted the issuance of the insurance policy bearing No.2312100935650900000 in respect of Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519 and the said policy was in force from 08.12.2020 to 07.12.2021 and the liability if any, shall be strictly subject to the terms and conditions Ramalingegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155464063/
2 of the policy and the petitioner has to put strict proof of the same.

sentences.text: It has also contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further contended that, the driver was driving the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519 without possessing a valid and SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.1466/2021 effective driving licence as on the date of the alleged accident and there was non-involvement of the insured vehicle in the said accident.
Further contended that, the accident occurred only due to sole negligence of the petitioner due to his old age.
Further this respondent denies the age, occupation and income of the petitioner and the expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following:
:: ISSUES::
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 17-02-2021 at about 01.35 p.m. while petitioner was riding a TVS XL bearing Reg.
No.KA-42-W-0966, when he reached NH-209, Near Jekkegowdana Doddi village, Sathanoor Hobli,
at that time the rider of the Fashion Pro Motor bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519 ridden in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle, as a result of which petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injury, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so, from which respondent?
SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.1466/2021 3. What Order or Award?

He has also examined his witnesses Dr.Avinash Parthasarathy as PW.2 and got marked four documents as Ex.P.21 to Ex.P.24.
On the other hand, riders of offending vehicle has examined as RW.1 and RW.2.
Ex.R.1 is marked through RW.1.
Assistant Manager, Legal of Insurance company has examined as RW.3 and got marked two documents as Ex.R.2 and Ex.R.3, Ex.P.4(a) and Ex.P.5(a) has confronted to RW.2 and closed their side evidence.
6. Heard the arguments from both sides.
Perused the entire records.

sentences.text: In order to prove the actionable negligence, the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1.
He has got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.
He has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed for his examination- in-chief.
9. It is relevant to note that the respondent No.1 has specifically contended that accident occurred only due to sole negligence of the petitioner due to old age.

The respondent also contended that,
complaint lodged after lapse of one day from the date of accident.

Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of rider of Fashion Pro Motor bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04- HB-2519.
10.

Petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and in his evidence has stated that on 17.02.2021 at about 1.35 pm., when he was riding a TVA XL bearing No.KA-42-W- 0966 on NH-209, Near Jekkegowdana Doddi village, Sathnoor Hobli carefully and cautiously and by observing SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.1466/2021 all the traffic rules on left side of the road, at that time, one Fashion Pro motor bike bearing No.KA-04-HB-2519 ridden by its rider with very high speed in a rash and negligent manner came from behind and dashed against him.
As a result he fell down along with TVS XL and sustained comminuted fracture end right leg both bone and other injuries all over the body.

11. PW.1 in support of his version, he has produced the certified copy of FIR with statement,
statement, mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, discharge summary, charge sheet and medical bills and got them marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.3, 6 to 9 and 16.
12.
I have perused Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.3, 6 to 9 and 16.

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 17.02.2021 at about 1.35 p.m. and the FIR at Ex.P.1 in crime No.0033/2021 came to be registered on 18.02.2021 at around 16.30, at Sathnoor Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC along with complaint which was lodged by wife of petitioner on 18.02.2021, Ex.P.3 - mahazar reveals that on spot of SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.1466/2021 accident is NH - 209, Kanakapura - Malavalli main road.
The IMV report marked at Ex.P.6 reveals that the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.

Further the records reveal that thereafter the police conducted investigation and filed charge-sheet at Ex.P.9 against the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC.
13.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross-examination of PW-1.
In his cross-examination PW.1 denied that the injury sustained by him due to self fall and not by the accident.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term Ramalingegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155464063/

sentences.text: "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.1466/2021 "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
14. On the other hand, riders of offending vehicle has been examined as RW.1 and RW.2 and through RW.1 and Rw-2 , Ex.R.1 and Ex.P-4(a) and 5 (a) has got marked.
During cross examination they have admitted the accident, but the accident occurred in another motor cycle.
But Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.9 are discloses that the accident occurred in the negligence of rider of the offending motorcycle.
that they have not challenged the charge sheet and also admitted the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of rider of the offending motor cycle which belongs to the respondent No.2.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2:
AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME: PW.1 has produced his Aadhar card at Ex.P.10.
As per this document, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 01.01.1959.
Therefore, as on the date of accident he was aged about 62 years.

Therefore,
the appropriate multiplier for the said age group as per Sarla Verma's case is '7'.
16.

The petitioner has deposed that prior to accident, he was doing agriculture work growing ragi,
vegetables and cocoons and earning sum of Rs.15,000/- per month owning 3 acres of land.

Along with oral suggestion to prove his income he has produced 3 computerized RTC which is standing in his name marked at Ex.P.12 to 14, 8 cocoons auction bills marked at Ex.P.15 and Ex.P.17 - 5 vehicle transport bills of Rs.17,500/-.
On perusal of Ex.P.15 and Ex.P.17, it can be assume his income may be at Rs.20,000/- to Rs.25,000/- per month.
But he has not produced his bank statement or he has not examined any witness to SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.1466/2021 prove the same.
Therefore, it is necessary to take into account notional income of the petitioner while calculating the compensation.
As per the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Service Authority the notional income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.15,000/- as the accident took place in the year 2021.

17. PW.1 has deposed that after the accident he was taken to Kanakapura Government Hospital after first aid treatment he was taken to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as inpatient for 2 months.

As per Ex-P6 - wound certificate petitioner sustained CLW with right leg,
tenderness over right leg and X-ray shows fracture of both bones of right leg.
Doctor opines that the above injury is grievous in nature.

Petitioner has produced his 3 discharge summaries at Ex.P.8 of Sanjay Gandhi Hospital wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 17.02.2021 to 25.02.2021 i.e.,
for 9 days, from 21.07.2021 to 07.08.2021 i.e., for 18 days and from 16.02.2022 to SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.1466/2021 24.02.2022 i.e., for 9 days.

Therefore, it is clear that the petitioner took Ramalingegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155464063/
5 treatment as an inpatient for total period of 36 days.

sentences.text: 18. The petitioner in order to show his disability has examined Dr.Avinash Parthasarathy as PW.2.

He has filed affidavit for his examination in chief and deposed that on examination the petitioner complains of pain in right leg and ankle, stiffness in right knee and ankle, he is unable to walk or sit normally, climb stairs, squat, kneel and he has difficulty in doing his routine activities due to the said disabilities.
Petitioner sustained right both bone leg fracture with open type III wound.
He was admitted at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital on the same of accident and underwent surgery on 20.02.2021 - wound debridement with Ex FIX application for tibia and ORIF with plate and screws for fibula.
He was discharged on 25.02.2021.

Again he admitted to the hospital on 21.07.2021 to 07.08.2021 and underwent ORIF with plate and screws for tibia with bone grafting and plate removal and rusch nail application for fibula on SCCH - 26 14 MVC No.1466/2021 30.07.2021.
Again he was readmitted from 16.02.2022 to 24.02.2022 and underwent fibula Rusch nail removal on 18.02.2022.

On examination dated 15.09.2022 he found antalgic gait in right lower limb, tenderness around right ankle, operated scar over right lateral malleolus and medial malleolus and leg, arc of movement right ankle dorsiflexion/plantar flexion restricted, difficulty in walking, climbing stairs, squatting,
sitting cross legged turning and kneeling and X-ray done on 15.09.2022 which shows malunited right tibia fracture with non-union fibula fracture with implants in situ.
PW.2 assessed whole body disability at 20%.
Further contended that, petitioner has restricted ROM in right knee and ankle along with pain in right leg and ankle.
He has difficulty in performing routine physical activities.
He has 20% whole body disability due to permanent physical impairment in right lower limb.
The disability is permanent in nature and interferes with routine physical activities.
The petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants and the SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.1466/2021 estimated cost of the said procedures in their hospital would be at Rs.15,000/-.

Along with his evidence he has produced 3 case sheets, disability assessment proforma, OP file and 2 X-rays marked at Ex.P.21 to 24.
19.
During cross examination he has deposed that he has not given treatment personally to the petitioner and not given any follow up treatment.
I did only disability assessment.
Petitioner has tibia fracture mal union and fibula fracture nonunion.
Surgery done for tibia and fibula.

From leg to ankle implants were fixed.
20.

It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

But in the present case, though the petitioner has got examined the doctor as PW.2 to show his disability, but the documents placed on record shows that he has the physical disability at 20% to the whole body.
But by SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.1466/2021 looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.

Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 12%
disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
21. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner has undergone pain and sufferings to some extent.
Thus, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

sentences.text: LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:

Considering the age, nature of injuries, treatment given as inpatient in the hospital and as an outpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least 3 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.45,000/- (15,000/- x 3) under this head.
23. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
As already stated supra the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for nearly 36 days as it could be seen from Ex.P.8.
It is SCCH - 26 17 MVC No.1466/2021 relevant to note that the petitioner has not produced documents to show that he took follow-up treatment.
Therefore, this tribunal inclines to award Rs.36,000/- under this head.
24. MEDICAL EXPENSES:-
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.16 - 29 medical bills of Rs.28,729/-.
Petitioner has also produced Ex.P.17 - 5 vehicle transport bills.
Ex.P.17 shows the traveling expenses incurred by the petitioner to go to hospital to take treatment.
Though Insurance Company not disputed the medical expenses and transport expenses and it appears to be genuine.

Hence,
Petitioner is awarded to Rs.46,229/- (Rs.28,729/- (+) Rs.17,500/-) towards Medical Expenses including transport bill.
25. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As on the date of accident he was aged about 62 years.
Therefore, the appropriate multiplier for the said age group as per Sarla Verma's case is '7'.

This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/-
p.m.
Hence, a sum of SCCH - 26 18 MVC No.1466/2021 Rs.1,51,200/- (Rs.15,000 X 12 X 7 X 12/100) is awarded under this head.
26. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face disappointment and frustration & also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures and joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.

27. The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Pain and sufferings 25,000=00 2 Loss of income during 45,000=00 laid-up period 3 Attendant charges, extra 36,000=00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 4
Medical expenses 46,229=00 5 Loss of future income due 1,51,200=00 to disability 6 Loss of future amenities & 25,000=00 happiness

Hence,
the petitioner is entitled for total SCCH - 26 19 MVC No.1466/2021 compensation of Rs.3,28,429/-.
28.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it Ramalingegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155464063/
7 would meet the ends of justice.

sentences.text: The main contention of the respondent No.1 that the rider of offending vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519 riding the same without possessing a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the alleged accident.
In order to prove the same an Assistant Manager, Legal has examined as RW.3 on behalf of respondent.
Through him got marked Ex.R.2 - policy and Ex.R.3 - investigation report.
Moreover, as admitted by the RW.1 that they have not challenged the final report.

In the absence of challenging the same, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the RC owner of offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a.
The SCCH - 26 20 MVC No.1466/2021 primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
29. ISSUE NO.3:

For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following :-
-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,28,429/- (Rupees Three lakh twenty eight thousand four hundred twenty nine only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1 being insurer of offending motor cycle is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
After the deposit of entire compensation amount, entire compensation shall be SCCH - 26 21 MVC No.1466/2021 released in favour of petitioner through E-payment upon proper verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw an award accordingly.

Respondent No.1 - Insurance Company filed its objection that the denying the petition averments.
It has also contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further contended that, the driver was driving the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519 without possessing a valid and SCCH - 26 5 MVC No.1466/2021 effective driving licence as on the date of the alleged accident and there was non-involvement of the insured vehicle in the said accident.

Further contended that, the accident occurred only due to sole negligence of the petitioner due to his old age.

opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following:
:: ISSUES::
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 17-02-2021 at about 01.35 p.m. while petitioner was riding a TVS XL bearing Reg.
No.KA-42-W-0966, when he reached NH-209, Near Jekkegowdana Doddi village, Sathanoor Hobli,
at that time the rider of the Fashion Pro Motor bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519 ridden in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle, as a result of which petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injury, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of rider of Fashion Pro Motor bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04- HB-2519.
10.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Moreover, it is settled law that the term Ramalingegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155464063/
4
"rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.1466/2021 "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
But in the present case, though the petitioner has got examined the doctor as PW.2 to show his disability, but the documents placed on record shows that he has the physical disability at 20% to the whole body.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 12%
disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.
Ramalingegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155464063/
6 22.

7 would meet the ends of justice.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In the absence of challenging the same, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the RC owner of offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HB-2519 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a.
The SCCH - 26 20 MVC No.1466/2021 primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
29. ISSUE NO.3:
For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following :-
-: ORDER :-
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,28,429/- (Rupees Three lakh twenty eight thousand four hundred twenty nine only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1 being insurer of offending motor cycle is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
After the deposit of entire compensation amount, entire compensation shall be SCCH - 26 21 MVC No.1466/2021 released in favour of petitioner through E-payment upon proper verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw an award accordingly.
